newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher, near day's peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher, near day's peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures upticked again late to end stronger and near the day's highs.
But traders said afternoon activity remained languid, with the market showing muted upside response despite a five-year Treasury note auction that brokers considered well received.
The five-year note produced a high yield of 6.409 percent, a 2.57 bid/cover, and $477 million in non-competitive bids.
Dealers had expected a 6.41 percent yield, and some brokers said they had heard talk it might be slightly higher.
"We were hearing 6.41-plus," said one floor broker before the auction results were announced.
Immediately after the paper was sold, December T-bond futures ticked up to 109-30/32, within one tick of the day's high and a couple ticks shy of resistance at 110-00.
But momentum never materialized, and the contract returned to its afternoon range before firming again into the close.
"The market just lost its interest after that (auction)," a Eurodollar broker added. "We went offered, and that was it."
Some brokers were surprised by tepid reaction to the sale.
"It was a good auction," said one floor bank broker. "We should have rallied more. It's (scant response) due to lethargy, and nobody cares."
She said the market likely had already priced in a good sale during the morning's advance, and buyers hesitated as they perused this week's already hefty price gains.
"I think people were anticipating a pretty good auction, but not this good," she added. "But I think we've come so far up they've already got it (good auction priced) in them."
December T-bond futures on Monday hit the week's low at 107-14/32 and since have rallied by just over 2-1/2 points to Thursday's high at 109-31/32.
Futures jumped early after August U.S. durable goods orders fell 3.1 percent and lost 3.5 percent ex-defense.
Traders had expected a 0.1-percent overall decline and a 0.7-percent fall without defense orders.
December Euros early hurdled key resistance at 94.25 but on thin volume. Next resistance stood at 94.28, a double-top from mid-August that brokers said was also hit on low volume.
Traders noted some good-size buying from a couple of banks early in T-bonds and 10-year notes before the note sale.

At settlement, Dec T-bonds were up 19/32 at 109-26/32, T-notes gained 10/32 to 107-21/32, muni-bonds rose 19/32 to 114-17/32, Dec T-bills gained two bps to 94.81, and Eurodollars advanced two bps to 94.24. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
